html:
The Westo were a powerful and feared Native American people of the 1600s Southeast, who probably spoke an Iroquoian language. They seem to have come from the north, perhaps from the Erie of the Great Lakes, driven south during the Beaver Wars. They appear first in colonial Virginia.

Armed with guns from Virginia traders, they settled on the Savannah River near present Augusta, and raided Spanish missions in Guale and Apalachee and other peoples for captives, whom they sold to the English as slaves. The new colony of Carolina at first traded with them, but in 1680 its traders backed a war in which the colonists and Shawnee newcomers nearly wiped them out. Other peoples then took over the Indian slave trade, a chain of raiding that led to the Yamasee War of 1715.
